title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 3

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When does the talk begin?
tasks.audioText: The technology department will host a talk about renewable energy systems on Friday morning. The speaker will compare solar panels and wind turbines and explain why output changes with weather conditions. The talk begins at ten fifteen in Lecture Room 2. Students should read the short introduction on the college platform before attending.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. What should students read beforehand?
tasks.audioText: The technology department will host a talk about renewable energy systems on Friday morning. The speaker will compare solar panels and wind turbines and explain why output changes with weather conditions. The talk begins at ten fifteen in Lecture Room 2. Students should read the short introduction on the college platform before attending.
options: The short introduction on the college platform

tasks.prompt: A small community centre installed solar panels to reduce the electricity it bought from the grid. The panels produce the most energy on bright days, so the centre still uses grid electricity in the evening and during periods of low sunlight. The project report compares monthly production with consumption rather than claiming that the building is completely energy independent. It also recommends improving insulation to reduce demand. Reading 1. Why does the centre still use grid electricity?
options: Solar output varies and is lower in the evening or when sunlight is limited

tasks.prompt: What additional improvement does the report recommend?
Electricity demand can be reduced if buildings ___ more effectively.
Choose TWO factors that can affect solar energy production.
options: The colour of the classroom walls
The number of books in the library
The position and condition of the panels

tasks.prompt: Energy sources that are naturally replaced are called ___.
A classmate claims solar panels produce the same amount of energy every day. What is a suitable response?
options: That is not quite correct; output can change with sunlight and weather.
All energy systems work in exactly the same way.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of renewable energy in a logical order.
Write 80–100 words comparing two renewable energy sources. Explain one advantage and one limitation of each.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: two renewable energy sources are identified and compared (0–2); one relevant advantage and one limitation are explained for each source (0–2); comparative language and logical links are understandable (0–2); energy/environment vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
